facts.label: Version relationships and conflicts
facts.text: 1. Share count at 2025-12-31. The annual report cover states "As at December 31, 2025, 395,521,903 common shares were outstanding" (40-F page:1). The 2026 interim share capital note shows "Balance, beginning of year 396,834,231" and the same figure in the "Year ended Dec. 31, 2025" column (Q2 statements page:23; Q1 statements page:17). The MD&A reports 396,148,639 shares on 2025-11-10 (MD&A page:46). Downstream effect: per-share, dilution and any equity-value inputs depend on which count is used. The statement note is the filed IFRS source; the 40-F cover is a registrant representation. The sources do not explain the gap, so it is carried as an unresolved conflict. 2. Free cash flow history changed between releases. Fourth quarter 2025 free cash flow is 228.2 with cash sustaining capital expenditures of 108.7 in the February release (release FY2025 page:10-11 and page:41), but 225.0 with 111.9 in the May and July releases (release Q1 page:25; release Q2 page:25). The community agreement cash payments line moves from 4.4 to 7.6 for the same quarter. Third quarter 2025 free cash flow is (15.2) in the MD&A and the February release but (16.1) in the later releases. Downstream effect: any free cash flow series must name the release version and cannot splice versions. 3. Internal inconsistency in the July release. Its trailing table prints fourth quarter 2025 "Cash generated from operations" of 290.4 (release Q2 page:25), while the May release prints 209.4 for that quarter (release Q1 page:25) and the July release's own twelve-month total of 831.2 equals the sum using 209.4 (see Calculations). Its free cash flow of 225.0 for that quarter also agrees with 209.4. The 290.4 figure is therefore not usable until confirmed; the 209.4 figure is used as the consistent value. 4. Municipal bond maturity wording. The statements say the bonds have "an initial mandatory tender date of July 2, 2036" (Q2 statements page:14), while the July release says "solid waste disposal revenue bonds due July 2, 2036" (release Q2 page:18). The final legal maturity is not stated. Downstream effect: the maturity wall for these bonds cannot be placed without the bond terms. 5. Wheaton stream status. The November 2025 MD&A says Hudbay "agreed on terms with Wheaton Precious Metals Corp." to amend the Copper World streaming agreement (MD&A page:5). The February and July 2026 releases both list, among forward-looking items, "the ability to consummate the definitive agreement with Wheaton" and "the benefits, timing and consummation of the definitive agreement with Wheaton" (release FY2025 page:50; release Q2 page:32). The pack does not state whether the definitive agreement was signed. This is a stated uncertainty, not a numeric conflict.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: On reported figures Hudbay is lightly leveraged and strongly cash generative, but its liquidity structure changed materially in Q2 2026. Trailing adjusted EBITDA reached 1,271.6 at 2026-06-30, the highest of the five trailing quarter-ends in the pack (995.7, 932.3, 1,060.9, 1,195.6 and 1,271.6). Total long-term debt was 860.2, down from 1,008.6 at 2025-12-31, so the ratio of debt to trailing adjusted EBITDA was 0.68 times on carrying value, against 0.95 times at 2025-12-31. The company's own net debt was negative 80.5, which would read as net cash. That headline needs three qualifications. First, cash of 890.9 includes 334.5 held by Copper World LLC, which the company says is contractually restricted to the Copper World project. Second, the company deducts a further 49.8 of restricted bond proceeds. Third, those proceeds come from the 52.0 of municipal bonds, which are debt of Copper World LLC guaranteed by the company. If Copper World cash, the restricted proceeds and the bonds are all set aside, net debt for the rest of the group is 253.1, or 0.20 times (derived in Calculations). The composition of liquidity changed: undrawn revolver was 153.7 at 2026-06-30 against 425.2 at 2026-03-31, because the 2026 notes of 472.5 were repaid on 2026-04-01 using cash and a 272.0 revolver draw. Headline liquidity of 1,044.6 compares with 956.5 that the company gave for 2026-03-31 after the repayment (PR-Q1 page:6). The next funded maturities are the revolver draw at its November 2028 facility maturity and the 6.125% notes of 542.4 due April 2029. The earnings base is strong but not cheap to convert to cash: Q2 2026 tax expense was 102.3 on pre-tax income of 240.4, and six-month taxes paid were 262.8. Earnings fell between Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 (adjusted EBITDA 421.9 to 321.2), which management attributes to lower sales volumes after port closures in Peru delayed shipments that were delivered in July. The base has five limits. No covenant level or ratio is printed. The audited FY2025 statements are not supplied, so FY2025 figures come from a management release. Cash interest for a full year is not printed. Facility-level revolver availability is not printed. The free cash flow history differs between releases.

That makes Q2 operating cash flow of 297.0 a partly timing-driven figure; operating cash flow before working capital, 210.1, is the cleaner series and was essentially flat on Q1 (208.7). Taxes paid were 262.8 for six months against 161.4 a year earlier. Cash taxes equal 35.4% of six-month adjusted EBITDA (derived). Six-month capital spending on property, plant and equipment was 293.1 against 213.1. Free cash flow on the company definition was 101.8 in Q2 and 102.3 in Q1, so 204.1 for the half (derived). Net purchase of investments of 38.7 sits outside that definition (Q2FS page:3). Dividends are small, 5.7 for six months.

facts.label: Liquidity
facts.text: Company total liquidity of 1,044.6 is cash of 890.9 plus 153.7 of undrawn revolver. Of the cash, 334.5 is held by Copper World LLC under contractual restriction (PR-Q2 page:25) and is not available to the rest of the group. Cash excluding it is 556.4, and liquidity on the same basis is 710.1 (derived). Undrawn availability fell from 425.2 to 153.7 over the quarter and the facilities are now 65.8% used including letters of credit: (272.0 + 24.3) / 450.0 (derived). The sources do not say how the 450.0 divides between the Canadian and Peruvian facilities. Because the draw and the letters of credit sit on the Canadian facility, the company's 153.7 is an aggregate that holds only if the Canadian commitment exceeds 296.3 (derived) or the facilities can be combined; neither is printed. Neither facility matures within twelve months. Restricted municipal bond proceeds of 49.8 are classified as current and expected to be drawn within twelve months (Q2FS page:14). Near-term cash demands visible in the filings: about 30 million at Cactus and about 20 million of Mason evaluation spending in the second half of 2026 (PR-Q2 page:19, page:22), capital commitments of 202.6 of which 18.7 is not terminable (derived), and the July dividend declaration of C$0.01 per share (PR-Q2 page:22). The company states that current liquidity and operating cash flow should be sufficient for the remainder of 2026 (PR-Q2 page:6), a management statement.

facts.label: Earnings quality and definitions
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA differs from IFRS earnings in several recurring ways: it deducts 9.5 of amortization of deferred revenue in Q2 (non-cash stream revenue), adds back 10.2 of share-based compensation, and starts from net earnings after a finance subtotal that was a net credit of 20.7 in Q2 because of 48.7 of fair-value gains on investments and share-based compensation instruments (Q2FS page:12-13 and PR-Q2 page:24). Mark-to-market gains of 38.2 are excluded from adjusted net earnings (PR-Q2 page:24), so reported net income of 138.1 includes gains that adjusted net earnings attributable to owners of 113.5 does not. The effective tax rate was 42.6% in Q2 2026 and 43.1% for six months (derived), reflecting mining taxes of 32.7 current and 1.4 deferred in Q2 alongside income tax (Q2FS page:22). Revenue includes pricing and volume adjustments of negative 36.7 in Q2, mark-to-market on provisionally priced sales (Q2FS page:10); the net position awaiting final pricing was a liability of 9.5 at 2026-06-30 (Q2FS page:29). Q2 gross profit ties to the segment note. Gold and silver stream deferred revenue of 297.1 is amortised into revenue without cash; 9.5 was amortised in Q2 (Q2FS page:10, page:20).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Hudbay is a Canadian-incorporated, listed copper and gold producer with three operating regions (Constancia in Peru, the Snow Lake operations in Manitoba and Copper Mountain in British Columbia), one care-and-maintenance site (Flin Flon) and a US development pipeline (Copper World and Cactus in Arizona, Mason in Nevada). For a creditor the operating model has three features that matter. First, revenue is concentrate and doré sold at provisional prices that are finally set up to about three months later, so quarterly revenue and working capital move with metal prices and shipment timing, as the second-quarter port closures in Peru showed. Second, gold and silver by-product credits lower reported unit costs and add a stream obligation: part of revenue is non-cash amortisation of deferred revenue from precious metals streaming agreements. Third, the group is moving from de-leveraging to growth: the 2026 events are the sale of 30% of Copper World to Mitsubishi, the all-share acquisition of Arizona Sonoran, the repayment of the 2026 notes with cash and a revolver draw, and 52.0 of municipal bonds issued by the Copper World entity. The structural point is that Copper World, Mason and now Cactus are excluded from the guarantee of the senior notes and from the security for the revolving facilities, yet the municipal bonds issued by Copper World LLC carry a parent guarantee. Project cash of 334.5 is contractually restricted to Copper World. So value and cash are being built in assets that sit outside the existing creditor collateral, while the parent keeps a contingent exposure to their debt. Ownership: no controlling or sponsor holder is disclosed in the sources; the context names no sponsor. The behaviour record is supportive on documented actions (debt repurchases below par, repayment at maturity, no distributions beyond a small dividend), with a policy statement of net debt to adjusted EBITDA below 1.0x through the investment cycle, which is management language and not a covenant. Legal capacity cannot be assessed because no indenture or credit agreement is supplied. The Wheaton enhanced stream for Copper World is described as agreed in terms but, in the latest release, still as a definitive agreement to be consummated, so project funding sources remain partly unfixed.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Copper World joint venture. Hudbay sold a 30% minority interest in Copper World to Mitsubishi Corporation under a subscription agreement dated 2025-08-12; the transaction closed in January 2026. Mitsubishi paid about 420 at closing (422.7 was recorded as received) and will pay a further 180.0 within 18 months of closing, plus 30% of future equity contributions. Hudbay keeps 70% and consolidates Copper World. The deal is accounted for as an equity transaction: a non-controlling interest of 461.6 was recognised, a deferred consideration receivable of 169.8 accretes toward 180.0, and the closing cash is restricted to the project. Stated use of the closing proceeds is to fund the remaining feasibility study, pre-sanction costs and initial development. Status: closed; the second payment is outstanding. Creditor effect: the closing cash (334.5 still held at 2026-06-30 by the project entity) is not available to other creditors, and the receivable belongs to the project.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Copper World feasibility and sanction. The feasibility study is described as progressing well with 95% of engineering complete and a sanction decision on track for late 2026. The study "is expected to reflect higher capital expenditures as compared to the 2023 pre-feasibility study primarily due to typical cost inflation along with new capital related to project scope changes that would allow for future mill expansion optionality" (PR-Q2 page:18). Earlier releases gave a feasibility completion date of mid-2026 (PR-Q1 page:16; PR-FY25 page:23); the July release gives no completion date. The 2023 pre-feasibility funding assumptions included 350 of project-level financing and 230 from a precious metals stream (Q3MDA page:9, footnote 4), which are management assumptions that predate the joint venture and the new study. Status: pending. Creditor effect: sanction will draw on project cash, partner contributions, the stream and possibly project-level debt; any project debt that carries a parent guarantee would be a new claim on the group, as the municipal bonds already are.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Arizona Sonoran acquisition. Hudbay acquired all shares of Arizona Sonoran Copper Company Inc. not already owned, at 0.242 of a Hudbay share per share, by plan of arrangement completed 2026-06-24. It issued 46,794,082 shares and cancelled its existing stake valued at 123.1, recorded net identifiable assets of 1,267.0 and treated the purchase as an asset acquisition because substantially all value is in the Cactus project (Q2FS page:8). It assumed deferred land payments of 102.8 at 6% interest that are secured vendor carryback loans with deeds of trust (Q2FS page:16): 5.0 a year in 2026 to 2028 and 82.2 on 2029-08-28, prepayable without penalty. Hudbay expects to spend about 30 at Cactus in the second half of 2026 on an updated pre-feasibility study and site work (PR-Q2 page:4). Status: closed. Creditor effect: no corporate debt was issued and 46,794,082 new shares dilute equity, but the project is outside the guarantee and security perimeter, adds secured land debt, and competes with Copper World for capital after sanction.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Hudbay Minerals Inc. has a sound fundamental credit profile today, with low leverage and strong cash generation, but the profile is exposed to thin committed liquidity and to a large Arizona capital programme. The strongest support is total debt of USD 860.2 million against trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,271.6 million (0.68x), no funded maturity before 2028, and earnings spread over three mines, two countries of operation and several metals. The weakest point is liquidity: undrawn revolver of USD 153.7 million after the April 2026 draw, and USD 334.5 million of cash restricted to Copper World, so that cash available to the rest of the group is USD 556.4 million. The outcome will be decided by the Copper World sanction decision expected in late 2026 and how it is funded, by the gold price that supports by-product credits, and by covenant terms that are not supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Hudbay Minerals Inc. reported total long-term debt of USD 860.2 million at 2026-06-30, down from USD 1,008.6 million at 2025-12-31, while trailing adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,271.6 million, the highest of the five trailing quarter-ends in the financial base. ### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations. All four requested consumers are assessed as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, none CONDITIONAL and none BLOCKED. The pack holds two sets of filed unaudited interim statements with notes (first and second quarter 2026), one filed MD&A (third quarter 2025), the annual report cover document, and three management news releases that together cover the fourth quarter and full year 2025 and the first and second quarters of 2026. All are in USD, the context's reporting currency, and all are dated on or before 2026-07-29, inside the cutoff. The binding limitations are five. First, the audited FY2025 statements, annual information form and annual MD&A are incorporated by the annual report but not supplied, so FY2025 income and cash flow figures come from a news release and the 2025-12-31 balance sheet comes from interim comparatives. Second, no indenture, credit agreement or other executed legal document is supplied, so covenant levels, guarantor lists, security and borrower identity rest on filing summaries. Third, nothing dated after 2026-07-29 is supplied, so events between that date and the cutoff are Not supplied, not absent. Fourth, the text extraction has had no fidelity review and charts or images were not inspected. Fifth, three cross-source conflicts (listed below) must be carried forward by name. None of these prevents a consumer from starting.

### Financial base view

On reported figures Hudbay is lightly leveraged and strongly cash generative, but its liquidity structure changed materially in Q2 2026. Trailing adjusted EBITDA reached 1,271.6 at 2026-06-30, the highest of the five trailing quarter-ends in the pack (995.7, 932.3, 1,060.9, 1,195.6 and 1,271.6). Total long-term debt was 860.2, down from 1,008.6 at 2025-12-31, so the ratio of debt to trailing adjusted EBITDA was 0.68 times on carrying value, against 0.95 times at 2025-12-31. The company's own net debt was negative 80.5, which would read as net cash. That headline needs three qualifications. First, cash of 890.9 includes 334.5 held by Copper World LLC, which the company says is contractually restricted to the Copper World project. Second, the company deducts a further 49.8 of restricted bond proceeds. Third, those proceeds come from the 52.0 of municipal bonds, which are debt of Copper World LLC guaranteed by the company. If Copper World cash, the restricted proceeds and the bonds are all set aside, net debt for the rest of the group is 253.1, or 0.20 times (derived in Calculations). The composition of liquidity changed: undrawn revolver was 153.7 at 2026-06-30 against 425.2 at 2026-03-31, because the 2026 notes of 472.5 were repaid on 2026-04-01 using cash and a 272.0 revolver draw. Headline liquidity of 1,044.6 compares with 956.5 that the company gave for 2026-03-31 after the repayment (PR-Q1 page:6). The next funded maturities are the revolver draw at its November 2028 facility maturity and the 6.125% notes of 542.4 due April 2029. The earnings base is strong but not cheap to convert to cash: Q2 2026 tax expense was 102.3 on pre-tax income of 240.4, and six-month taxes paid were 262.8. Earnings fell between Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 (adjusted EBITDA 421.9 to 321.2), which management attributes to lower sales volumes after port closures in Peru delayed shipments that were delivered in July. ### Interpretation
#### Leverage

On the company's definitions the group moved from net debt of 439.7 at 2025-12-31 to negative 80.5 at 2026-06-30. Total long-term debt fell by 148.4 while cash rose by 322.0. The cash rise came from financing as well as operations: the sale of a 30% interest in Copper World brought in 411.7 net of costs (Q2FS page:3), and the company reports 334.5 of cash held at Copper World LLC at 2026-06-30. Trailing adjusted EBITDA was 995.7 at Q2 2025, fell to 932.3 at Q3 2025, then rose to 1,060.9, 1,195.6 and 1,271.6, so the debt ratio fell through both a lower numerator and a higher denominator since the Q3 2025 low. The ratio uses company adjusted EBITDA, which adds back share-based compensation and deducts amortization of deferred revenue, and is not a covenant measure. The principal view is slightly higher than carrying: 866.4 at 2026-06-30. A reader using debt plus leases plus equipment financing plus deferred land payments gets 1,147.3 (860.2 + 53.0 + 131.3 + 102.8, derived), or 0.90 times trailing adjusted EBITDA. The company's net debt excludes all four of those claims.

The February release says "reduced total principal debt to $1,008.6 million as of December 31, 2025" (PR-FY25 page:22). That figure is the carrying value of total long-term debt (Q2FS page:18). The principal at that date reconstructs to 1,014.9: the Q1 2026 note shows 1,014.9 of notes principal at 2026-03-31 with no repurchases in the quarter (Q1FS page:13), and the revolver was undrawn. This is an inference, because no source prints the 2025-12-31 principal. The release's wording is a label error, not a different number.
#### Coverage

Interest cover on a cash basis cannot be built for a full year because full-year interest paid is not printed. The six-month ratio of 24.77 times is very high and is probably overstated by timing: the cash flow statements show 30.0 of interest paid in Q2 2026 and no interest-paid line in Q1 2026, so the half-year appears to contain one coupon date for the notes (dates are not printed). On an accrual basis, interest expense on long term debt was 27.7 for six months 2026, equal to 26.83 times six-month adjusted EBITDA of 743.1 (derived). Accretion on streaming arrangements of 9.0 is a further non-cash charge. The revolver draw of 272.0 (April 2026) and the municipal bonds of 52.0 (24 June 2026) add interest cost: the bonds carry 4.50%, about 2.3 a year (derived), and the 6.125% notes carry about 33.2 a year on 542.4 (derived). The revolver rate is not printed, so the run-rate cost of the draw cannot be stated. Coupon dates are not printed.
#### Cash flow quality

Six-month cash generated from operating activities was 508.3 against 384.7 a year earlier, helped by a working capital inflow of 89.5 (27.3 in 2025), of which trade and other receivables contributed 175.5 (Q2FS page:29). The receivables inflow reverses part of the year-end build and the Q2 port-closure effect: trade receivables fell from 343.8 to 163.1 "primarily due to a delay in scheduled shipments in Peru impacted by the temporary port closures" (Q2FS page:13). That makes Q2 operating cash flow of 297.0 a partly timing-driven figure; operating cash flow before working capital, 210.1, is the cleaner series and was essentially flat on Q1 (208.7). Taxes paid were 262.8 for six months against 161.4 a year earlier. Cash taxes equal 35.4% of six-month adjusted EBITDA (derived). Six-month capital spending on property, plant and equipment was 293.1 against 213.1. Free cash flow on the company definition was 101.8 in Q2 and 102.3 in Q1, so 204.1 for the half (derived). Net purchase of investments of 38.7 sits outside that definition (Q2FS page:3). Dividends are small, 5.7 for six months.
#### Liquidity

Company total liquidity of 1,044.6 is cash of 890.9 plus 153.7 of undrawn revolver. Of the cash, 334.5 is held by Copper World LLC under contractual restriction (PR-Q2 page:25) and is not available to the rest of the group. Cash excluding it is 556.4, and liquidity on the same basis is 710.1 (derived). Undrawn availability fell from 425.2 to 153.7 over the quarter and the facilities are now 65.8% used including letters of credit: (272.0 + 24.3) / 450.0 (derived). The sources do not say how the 450.0 divides between the Canadian and Peruvian facilities. Because the draw and the letters of credit sit on the Canadian facility, the company's 153.7 is an aggregate that holds only if the Canadian commitment exceeds 296.3 (derived) or the facilities can be combined; neither is printed. Neither facility matures within twelve months. Restricted municipal bond proceeds of 49.8 are classified as current and expected to be drawn within twelve months (Q2FS page:14). Near-term cash demands visible in the filings: about 30 million at Cactus and about 20 million of Mason evaluation spending in the second half of 2026 (PR-Q2 page:19, page:22), capital commitments of 202.6 of which 18.7 is not terminable (derived), and the July dividend declaration of C$0.01 per share (PR-Q2 page:22). The company states that current liquidity and operating cash flow should be sufficient for the remainder of 2026 (PR-Q2 page:6), a management statement.

The Copper World joint venture also carries a receivable: Mitsubishi is to contribute 180.0 within 18 months of closing, recorded at 173.0 at 2026-06-30 (Q2FS page:9, page:13). That inflow is contractual, belongs to Copper World, and is not counted in liquidity.
#### Latest quarter and events after quarter-end

Financing events in Q2 2026: repayment of 472.5 of 4.50% notes on 2026-04-01; 272.0 revolver draw; 52.0 municipal bond issue on 2026-06-24; Arizona Sonoran acquisition completed 2026-06-24 for 46,794,082 shares valued at 1,135.6 plus Hudbay's existing stake of 123.1, net identifiable assets 1,267.0 including 102.8 of deferred land payments assumed and cash acquired of 63.0 (Q2FS page:8). Closing payments of 49.3 were made by Arizona Sonoran between 2026-06-24 and 2026-06-30 (page:8). The Copper World joint venture closed in January 2026 with cash of 422.7 received (Q2FS page:9). Insurance business interruption recovery of 11.5 was recorded and fully received (Q2FS page:11). Subsequent to quarter-end the documents show only: delivery in the first half of July of the delayed concentrate (about 10,000 dry metric tonnes), the dividend declaration of 2026-07-28, executive appointments, and the statement that the Copper World sanctioning decision is on track for late 2026 (PR-Q2 page:4-5, page:15, page:22). Amounts or events after 2026-07-29 are Not supplied.

Disasters and legal items: the interim statements contain no litigation or consent-decree note. The wildfire insurance recovery relates to 2025 Manitoba evacuations. The judicial review application by the Lower Similkameen Indian Band against the New Ingerbelle permit amendment is disclosed only in release narrative (PR-Q2 page:19; PR-Q1 page:15) with no financial amount.
#### Earnings quality and definitions

Adjusted EBITDA differs from IFRS earnings in several recurring ways: it deducts 9.5 of amortization of deferred revenue in Q2 (non-cash stream revenue), adds back 10.2 of share-based compensation, and starts from net earnings after a finance subtotal that was a net credit of 20.7 in Q2 because of 48.7 of fair-value gains on investments and share-based compensation instruments (Q2FS page:12-13 and PR-Q2 page:24). Mark-to-market gains of 38.2 are excluded from adjusted net earnings (PR-Q2 page:24), so reported net income of 138.1 includes gains that adjusted net earnings attributable to owners of 113.5 does not. The effective tax rate was 42.6% in Q2 2026 and 43.1% for six months (derived), reflecting mining taxes of 32.7 current and 1.4 deferred in Q2 alongside income tax (Q2FS page:22). Revenue includes pricing and volume adjustments of negative 36.7 in Q2, mark-to-market on provisionally priced sales (Q2FS page:10); the net position awaiting final pricing was a liability of 9.5 at 2026-06-30 (Q2FS page:29). Q2 gross profit ties to the segment note. Gold and silver stream deferred revenue of 297.1 is amortised into revenue without cash; 9.5 was amortised in Q2 (Q2FS page:10, page:20).

Definition risks carried forward: the free cash flow history differs between the February release and the May and July releases (CP-0 conflict 2); the July release prints 290.4 for Q4 2025 cash generated from operations against 209.4 elsewhere and its own trailing total of 831.2 supports 209.4 (CP-0 conflict 3); the share count at 2025-12-31 differs between the 40-F cover and the interim share note (CP-0 conflict 1); the municipal bond final maturity is not stated (CP-0 conflict 4).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Hudbay is a listed, copper and gold producer with no controlling owner shown. Its credit story is changing from operating-mine cash flow to funding Arizona growth, with project assets held outside the bank and note security. | Medium | The indenture, credit agreements, Copper World joint venture contract and Wheaton agreement are not supplied, so legal capacity and project funding terms cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Copper, gold and by-products come from three operating regions, with gold giving a large by-product credit and Peru, Manitoba and British Columbia each carrying separate disruption risks. | Cash flow is diversified across metals and countries, but each region has had recent interruptions that delayed sales. | High |

| The Copper World project is 70% owned, its cash is restricted to the project, and the sanction decision is expected in late 2026 after a higher-cost study. | Cash and project funding sit outside the group's collateral, so sanction raises capital calls and possible guarantees on project debt. | High |

| The Arizona Sonoran acquisition closed on 2026-06-24 for shares, with no new corporate debt but 102.8 of secured deferred land payments assumed. | Growth was equity-funded, but it adds a second Arizona development asset that needs funding after the Copper World decision. | High |

| Documented actions show debt reduction, a first dividend increase and a share buyback authority with no purchases under the current one, but no covenant or indenture terms are available. | Behaviour looks creditor-supportive so far, yet capacity for distributions and asset transfers cannot be assessed. | Medium |

| Management quotes gold at 38% of second-quarter revenue, which the filed revenue note does not reproduce. | The gold sensitivity of revenue is probably larger than the headline suggests and needs a reconciled basis. | Low |
### Business and transaction view

Hudbay is a Canadian-incorporated, listed copper and gold producer with three operating regions (Constancia in Peru, the Snow Lake operations in Manitoba and Copper Mountain in British Columbia), one care-and-maintenance site (Flin Flon) and a US development pipeline (Copper World and Cactus in Arizona, Mason in Nevada). For a creditor the operating model has three features that matter. First, revenue is concentrate and doré sold at provisional prices that are finally set up to about three months later, so quarterly revenue and working capital move with metal prices and shipment timing, as the second-quarter port closures in Peru showed. Second, gold and silver by-product credits lower reported unit costs and add a stream obligation: part of revenue is non-cash amortisation of deferred revenue from precious metals streaming agreements. Third, the group is moving from de-leveraging to growth: the 2026 events are the sale of 30% of Copper World to Mitsubishi, the all-share acquisition of Arizona Sonoran, the repayment of the 2026 notes with cash and a revolver draw, and 52.0 of municipal bonds issued by the Copper World entity. The structural point is that Copper World, Mason and now Cactus are excluded from the guarantee of the senior notes and from the security for the revolving facilities, yet the municipal bonds issued by Copper World LLC carry a parent guarantee. Project cash of 334.5 is contractually restricted to Copper World. So value and cash are being built in assets that sit outside the existing creditor collateral, while the parent keeps a contingent exposure to their debt. Ownership: no controlling or sponsor holder is disclosed in the sources; the context names no sponsor. The behaviour record is supportive on documented actions (debt repurchases below par, repayment at maturity, no distributions beyond a small dividend), with a policy statement of net debt to adjusted EBITDA below 1.0x through the investment cycle, which is management language and not a covenant. Legal capacity cannot be assessed because no indenture or credit agreement is supplied. The Wheaton enhanced stream for Copper World is described as agreed in terms but, in the latest release, still as a definitive agreement to be consummated, so project funding sources remain partly unfixed.

| Restricted proceeds | Bond proceeds are not available outside the project | Documentary Fact | Q2FS page:14, "These funds are not available for general operational or debt service use by other entities within the Hudbay consolidated group" | Disclosure | Consistent with the ring-fence |

| Related parties | No related-party note or related-party transaction is disclosed in the interim statements | Insufficient Information | Search of Q1FS and Q2FS for related party; none found | Related-party leakage: no evidence either way | Absence in interim statements is not evidence of absence in the annual set |

| Stakeholder and permit challenge | A First Nation applied for judicial review of the New Ingerbelle permit amendment | Documentary Fact | PR-Q2 page:19, "the LSIB subsequently submitted an application for judicial review" | Regulatory and stakeholder risk | Outcome and any financial effect are not stated |

| Disclosure and controls | Management's report on internal control and the auditor's opinion are incorporated by reference; the audited exhibits are not supplied | Documentary Fact | 40-F page:3-4 | Disclosure quality | Annual evidence cannot be checked here |

| Management changes | Management announced a President and Chief Financial Officer appointment and a chief operating officer succession on 2026-07-29 | Documentary Fact | PR-Q2 page:15, "Eugene Lei has been appointed President and Chief Financial Officer" | Continuity (issuer-level role changes only) | Planned succession announced with results; no adverse inference |

Behaviour read: on documented actions the issuer reads as Supportive to Neutral or Mixed. Supportive: voluntary note repurchases and maturity repayment, no extraction through dividends, equity-funded acquisition, partner-funded project. Mixed: projects and their cash sit outside creditor collateral, the parent guarantees project bonds, and the buyback authority is renewed. Creditor-adverse actions (priming, uptiering, drop-downs, non-pro-rata exchanges, collateral release) are not documented in the pack, but the pack contains no credit document that would show whether they are permitted. This reading is not an investment view.

### Segments and concentration

This section is prose by design so that the operating model table above stays the single table under its selector. Segment gross profit for Q2 2026 is held in the financial base: Peru, Manitoba and British Columbia together supply all revenue; Copper World and Cactus supply none (Q2FS page:30). Peru had the largest segment revenue (273.3) and Manitoba the highest segment gross profit (146.3); British Columbia earned a thin gross profit (7.2). Concentration is therefore by mine and by metal, with no customer concentration disclosed in the interim statements (customer and offtake detail is in the annual information form, which is not supplied).
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Copper World joint venture. Hudbay sold a 30% minority interest in Copper World to Mitsubishi Corporation under a subscription agreement dated 2025-08-12; the transaction closed in January 2026. Mitsubishi paid about 420 at closing (422.7 was recorded as received) and will pay a further 180.0 within 18 months of closing, plus 30% of future equity contributions. Hudbay keeps 70% and consolidates Copper World. The deal is accounted for as an equity transaction: a non-controlling interest of 461.6 was recognised, a deferred consideration receivable of 169.8 accretes toward 180.0, and the closing cash is restricted to the project. Stated use of the closing proceeds is to fund the remaining feasibility study, pre-sanction costs and initial development. Status: closed; the second payment is outstanding. Creditor effect: the closing cash (334.5 still held at 2026-06-30 by the project entity) is not available to other creditors, and the receivable belongs to the project.

Copper World feasibility and sanction. The feasibility study is described as progressing well with 95% of engineering complete and a sanction decision on track for late 2026. The study "is expected to reflect higher capital expenditures as compared to the 2023 pre-feasibility study primarily due to typical cost inflation along with new capital related to project scope changes that would allow for future mill expansion optionality" (PR-Q2 page:18). Earlier releases gave a feasibility completion date of mid-2026 (PR-Q1 page:16; PR-FY25 page:23); the July release gives no completion date. The 2023 pre-feasibility funding assumptions included 350 of project-level financing and 230 from a precious metals stream (Q3MDA page:9, footnote 4), which are management assumptions that predate the joint venture and the new study. Status: pending. Creditor effect: sanction will draw on project cash, partner contributions, the stream and possibly project-level debt; any project debt that carries a parent guarantee would be a new claim on the group, as the municipal bonds already are.

Wheaton enhanced stream. In August 2025 Hudbay agreed terms to amend the Copper World streaming agreement, adding up to 70 of contingent payment on a mill expansion alongside the initial 230 deposit, with ongoing gold and silver payments set at 15% of spot prices (Q3MDA page:13). The latest release still lists the definitive agreement as to be consummated (PR-Q2 page:32). Status: terms agreed; definitive agreement not confirmed in the pack. Creditor effect: a stream is a prior claim on project revenue; its signing, size and delivery obligations are not supplied.

Arizona Sonoran acquisition. Hudbay acquired all shares of Arizona Sonoran Copper Company Inc. not already owned, at 0.242 of a Hudbay share per share, by plan of arrangement completed 2026-06-24. It issued 46,794,082 shares and cancelled its existing stake valued at 123.1, recorded net identifiable assets of 1,267.0 and treated the purchase as an asset acquisition because substantially all value is in the Cactus project (Q2FS page:8). It assumed deferred land payments of 102.8 at 6% interest that are secured vendor carryback loans with deeds of trust (Q2FS page:16): 5.0 a year in 2026 to 2028 and 82.2 on 2029-08-28, prepayable without penalty. Hudbay expects to spend about 30 at Cactus in the second half of 2026 on an updated pre-feasibility study and site work (PR-Q2 page:4). Status: closed. Creditor effect: no corporate debt was issued and 46,794,082 new shares dilute equity, but the project is outside the guarantee and security perimeter, adds secured land debt, and competes with Copper World for capital after sanction.

Repayment of the 2026 notes and revolver draw. The 4.50% notes of 472.5 were repaid at maturity on 2026-04-01 using cash and a 272.0 draw on the Canadian revolving credit facility (Q2FS page:18-19). Status: closed. Creditor effect: refinancing risk before 2028 was removed, but undrawn revolver availability fell to 153.7 and the drawn revolver now matures with the facility in November 2028.

New debt issue: municipal bonds. On 2026-06-24 the Arizona Industrial Development Authority issued Series 2026A solid waste disposal revenue bonds of 52.0 at 4.50%, interest paid semi-annually, with an initial mandatory tender date of 2036-07-02; Copper World LLC is the obligor and the parent and primary operating subsidiaries guarantee on a senior unsecured basis (Q2FS page:14, page:20). The proceeds of 49.8 are held in a trust account for qualifying Copper World solid waste disposal expenditure and are expected to be used within twelve months. Status: issued. Creditor effect: low-cost long-dated project debt, with a parent guarantee and restricted proceeds.

Copper Mountain minority purchase. On 2025-04-30 Hudbay bought the 25% minority interest in Copper Mountain Mine (BC) Ltd. for 4.5 in cash, seven annual deferred payments of 3.0 and up to five contingent payments of 3.75, taking ownership to 100% (Q2FS page:9-10). Status: closed. Creditor effect: removes a minority claim on British Columbia cash flow and adds small deferred and contingent payments through 2033.

Other items: the JOGMEC and Marubeni option agreement over three Flin Flon-area projects (PR-FY25 page:26) is an exploration funding arrangement and carries no debt. Use of proceeds, sources and uses, sponsor and any related fees for the Arizona Sonoran and joint venture transactions beyond the amounts above are not supplied.

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for Hudbay Minerals Inc., as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway, with an evidence cutoff of 2026-11-05. It combines the financial base (USD millions, Q2 2026 and FY2025) and the business and transaction register into one credit view for a committee. It gives no relative value, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Hudbay has a sound credit profile on reported figures: debt of USD 860.2 million against trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,271.6 million, no funded maturity before 2028. Thin committed liquidity and Arizona capital needs limit it. | Medium | Covenant levels, debt documents, ownership data and anything after 2026-07-29 are not supplied, and trailing earnings are the company's own non-GAAP measure. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt was 0.68x trailing adjusted EBITDA at 2026-06-30, against 0.95x at 2025-12-31, and the ratio would still be 0.20x after setting aside ring-fenced Copper World items. | Leverage leaves wide room for earnings to fall before debt looks heavy. | Medium |

| Undrawn revolver was USD 153.7 million after a USD 272.0 million draw, and USD 334.5 million of the USD 890.9 million cash is restricted to Copper World. | Liquidity for the rest of the group is thinner than the headline of USD 1,044.6 million. | High |

| Funded maturities of USD 272.0 million in 2028 and USD 542.4 million in 2029 fall close together, with none earlier. | Refinancing is a 2028 and 2029 task, supported by trailing free cash flow of USD 413.0 million and long mine lives. | Medium |

| Copper World, Mason and Cactus sit outside the note guarantees and revolver security, while the Copper World bonds carry a parent guarantee. | Value and cash build outside creditor collateral, and project debt can become a group claim. | High |

| Earnings depend on gold by-product credits and on three exposed mines, with a Copper World sanction decision and higher study capital cost due in late 2026. | A gold price fall or a large project commitment would test the current low leverage. | Medium |
### Credit view

Hudbay Minerals Inc. has a sound fundamental credit profile today, with low leverage and strong cash generation, but the profile is exposed to thin committed liquidity and to a large Arizona capital programme. The strongest support is total debt of USD 860.2 million against trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,271.6 million (0.68x), no funded maturity before 2028, and earnings spread over three mines, two countries of operation and several metals. The weakest point is liquidity: undrawn revolver of USD 153.7 million after the April 2026 draw, and USD 334.5 million of cash restricted to Copper World, so that cash available to the rest of the group is USD 556.4 million. The outcome will be decided by the Copper World sanction decision expected in late 2026 and how it is funded, by the gold price that supports by-product credits, and by covenant terms that are not supplied.
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | View | Category | Basis | Confidence |

| Overall fundamental credit view | Sound and improving on reported leverage, constrained by liquidity structure, project funding and missing legal documents | Analyst Interpretation | Financial base: leverage, liquidity and maturity tables; business register: structure and behaviour read | Medium |

| Leverage | Total debt 0.68x and company net debt negative (-0.06x) on trailing adjusted EBITDA; 0.64x total and 0.20x net after setting aside ring-fenced Copper World items | Documentary Fact for the ratios' inputs; Analyst Interpretation for the ring-fenced view | Financial base: Chart data: leverage | Medium |

| Interest cover | High on the half-year measure (24.77x on cash interest paid) but timing-distorted; a full-year cash measure is Not supplied | Insufficient Information for a full-year measure | Financial base: Chart data: interest cover | Low |

| Liquidity | Headline USD 1,044.6 million; USD 710.1 million after removing Copper World cash; undrawn revolver USD 153.7 million | Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the adjusted view | Financial base: Chart data: liquidity | Medium |
| Refinancing | No funded maturity until 2028; USD 814.4 million falls in 2028 and 2029 | Documentary Fact | Financial base: Chart data: debt maturities | Medium |

| Business risk | Diversified by mine and metal, long reserve-based mine lives, exposed to disruption events and to gold prices | Documentary Fact and Management Language | Business register: operating model and credit translations | Medium |

| Structure and creditor control | Project assets outside collateral; parent guarantees project bonds; no indenture or credit agreement supplied | Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on capacity | Business register: ownership, control and governance behaviour | Medium |
| Covenant headroom | Not assessable: only compliance statements exist | Insufficient Information | Financial base: gaps | Not assessable |
### Credit thesis

Hudbay's low reported leverage, long-lived diversified mines and no funded maturity before 2028 support a sound credit profile, provided that the Copper World and Cactus capital programme is funded without eroding the thin committed liquidity or pushing project debt back onto the group (Analyst Interpretation).
### Key findings

Hudbay Minerals Inc. reported total long-term debt of USD 860.2 million at 2026-06-30, down from USD 1,008.6 million at 2025-12-31, while trailing adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,271.6 million, the highest of the five trailing quarter-ends in the financial base. Total debt over trailing adjusted EBITDA was 0.68x, against 0.95x at 2025-12-31, and the company's own net debt was negative USD 80.5 million (Documentary Fact). The measure is the company's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, which adds back share-based compensation and deducts non-cash stream amortisation, and no covenant definition is supplied (Documentary Fact).

The headline net cash position needs three qualifications. USD 334.5 million of the USD 890.9 million cash is held by Copper World LLC and restricted to that project. USD 49.8 million of municipal bond proceeds are also restricted. The USD 52.0 million of bonds is Copper World debt that the parent guarantees. Setting those aside, total debt is 0.64x and net debt USD 253.1 million, or 0.20x, still low (Analyst Interpretation).

Liquidity changed shape in the second quarter. The company repaid USD 472.5 million of 4.50% notes at maturity on 2026-04-01 using cash and a USD 272.0 million revolver draw, so undrawn revolver availability fell from USD 425.2 million at 2026-03-31 to USD 153.7 million. Headline liquidity of USD 1,044.6 million is now mostly cash. The revolver split between its Canadian and Peruvian facilities is not printed, so the USD 153.7 million is an aggregate that may overstate what is usable on the facility that carries the draw (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on the split).

The next funded maturities are the USD 272.0 million revolver draw at its November 2028 facility maturity and USD 542.4 million of 6.125% notes due April 2029, with nothing earlier. Together they equal about two years of trailing free cash flow of USD 413.0 million (1.97x, derived), which is manageable if earnings hold, but the two maturities fall within five months of each other (Analyst Interpretation).

Cash conversion is strong but sensitive. First-half 2026 cash taxes paid were USD 262.8 million, equal to 35.4% of adjusted EBITDA, and the effective tax rate was 43.1%. Capital spending of USD 293.1 million took more than half of operating cash flow of USD 508.3 million. Free cash flow on the company definition was USD 204.1 million for the half, but the free cash flow history differs between releases (Documentary Fact; derived ratios in Calculations).

The business is diversified but exposed. Revenue comes from three operating regions with gold by-product credits that lower unit cost, and mine lives to 2040, 2041 and 2045 are management estimates. Recent interruptions include Peruvian unrest and Manitoba wildfires in 2025 and port closures in the second quarter of 2026 that delayed about 10,000 dry metric tonnes of concentrate (Documentary Fact; Management Language on mine lives).

The structure is the main creditor point. Copper World, Mason and Cactus are excluded from the note guarantees and from the revolver security, Copper World cash is restricted, and the parent guarantees the Copper World bonds. The Copper World sanction decision is expected in late 2026 after a feasibility study that management says will reflect higher capital cost than the 2023 study, the Wheaton enhanced stream is not confirmed as signed, and the Arizona Sonoran acquisition added USD 102.8 million of secured deferred land payments (Documentary Fact; Management Language on timing). Whether creditors' collateral and cash are diluted by this programme depends on documents that are not supplied.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Low leverage: total debt at 0.68x trailing adjusted EBITDA and a trend from 1.12x at 2025-09-30 (Documentary Fact for inputs). Cash generation: trailing free cash flow of USD 413.0 million on the company definition, with a first-half operating cash flow of USD 508.3 million (Documentary Fact). Maturity runway: no funded maturity before 2028 after the 2026 notes were repaid (Documentary Fact). Diversification: three operating regions, copper plus gold, with by-product credits and long reserve-based mine lives (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Documented behaviour: repurchases below par, repayment at maturity, an equity-funded acquisition, partner funding of 30% of Copper World, a very small dividend and no buyback purchases under the current authority (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation that behaviour is supportive to neutral).

Weaknesses. Committed liquidity: undrawn revolver of USD 153.7 million, 65.8% of the USD 450.0 million facilities used including letters of credit, and facility-level availability not printed (Documentary Fact; derived). Ring-fenced cash: USD 334.5 million not available to the wider group (Documentary Fact). Structural position: project assets outside collateral with a parent guarantee of project bonds (Documentary Fact). Project and capital intensity: Copper World sanction, higher study cost, the Cactus programme and New Ingerbelle spending ahead (Management Language). Earnings sensitivity: dependence on gold by-product credits, and a 43.1% effective tax rate on first-half income (Analyst Interpretation on sensitivity). Evidence quality: FY2025 figures from a management release, a misprinted trailing cell in the July release, a conflicting share count and no covenant levels (Insufficient Information on covenants).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Thin committed liquidity and facility-level availability | A USD 272.0 million draw and USD 24.3 million of letters of credit use 65.8% of the USD 450.0 million facilities; the split between the two facilities is not printed | Back-up liquidity is small relative to USD 860.2 million of debt and to project calls; group liquidity leans on cash that is partly restricted | Material |

| Ring-fenced cash and cash trapping | USD 334.5 million sits at Copper World LLC and USD 49.8 million of bond proceeds are restricted | Cash for other creditors is USD 556.4 million, not USD 890.9 million; net debt for the rest of the group is USD 253.1 million | Material |

| Project funding and parent recourse | Copper World sanction needs funding beyond Mitsubishi's 30%; the study capital cost is higher than in 2023; the Wheaton agreement is unconfirmed; the parent already guarantees USD 52.0 million of project bonds | New project debt with a parent guarantee would become a claim on the group while project assets are outside collateral | Material |

| Maturity concentration in 2028 and 2029 | USD 272.0 million (November 2028) and USD 542.4 million (April 2029) fall within five months | Refinancing needs to be completed by 2028; USD 814.4 million equals about two years of trailing free cash flow | Material |

| Metal price and gold dependence | By-product credits lower unit cost; stream amortisation is non-cash; the share of revenue from gold is disputed between management and the filed note | A gold price fall hits both revenue and cost offsets; a 32.4% fall in trailing adjusted EBITDA would lift total debt to 1.0x (derived) | Material |

| Operating event risk | Peruvian unrest, Manitoba wildfires and Peruvian port closures each delayed output or shipments within the last 12 months | Quarterly cash flow and working capital swing; a longer event would test liquidity | Material |

| Acquisition and development dilution | The all-share Arizona Sonoran purchase added a second Arizona development asset and USD 102.8 million of secured land payments | Competes with Copper World for capital after sanction; no new corporate debt so far | Minor |
| Cash tax intensity | Cash taxes were 35.4% of first-half adjusted EBITDA | Free cash flow is lower than EBITDA suggests; a tax change or timing swing moves cash | Minor |

| Covenant and documentation opacity | No covenant level, indenture or credit agreement is supplied | Headroom and permitted-payment capacity cannot be tested; missing evidence is not an adverse finding | Material |
## Calculations
Inputs are US$ millions from the financial base unless stated. All results are derived arithmetic on cited upstream figures.
| Item | Formula and inputs | Result |
| Total debt to trailing adjusted EBITDA | 860.2 / 1,271.6 | 0.68x |
| Cash available outside Copper World | 890.9 - 334.5 | 556.4 |
| Liquidity outside Copper World | 556.4 + 153.7 | 710.1 |
| Undrawn revolver as a share of total debt | 153.7 / 860.2 | 17.9% |
| Cash outside Copper World as a share of total debt | 556.4 / 860.2 | 64.7% |
| Revolver use including letters of credit | (272.0 + 24.3) / 450.0 | 65.8% |
| Funded maturities in 2028 and 2029 | 272.0 + 542.4 | 814.4 |
| 2028 and 2029 maturities against trailing free cash flow | 814.4 / 413.0 | 1.97 times |
| Maturities in 2028 and 2029 against liquidity outside Copper World | 710.1 / 814.4 | 0.87 times |
| Earnings fall that lifts total debt to 1.0x | 1 - 860.2 / 1,271.6 | 32.4% |
| Total debt to adjusted EBITDA after a 25% earnings fall, debt unchanged | 860.2 / (1,271.6 x 0.75) | 0.90x |
| First-half adjusted EBITDA less cash sustaining capital expenditures | 321.2 + 421.9 - 108.3 - 106.4 | 528.4 |
| That amount over first-half interest expense on long term debt | 528.4 / 27.7 | 19.08x (accrual basis) |
| Trailing free cash flow over total debt | 413.0 / 860.2 | 48.0% |
| Lease-adjusted debt over trailing adjusted EBITDA | 1,147.3 / 1,271.6 | 0.90x |
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | What it affects | Severity | Action |

| Covenant levels, step-downs, ratios and headroom are Not supplied; only compliance statements exist | Headroom against the revolver tests cannot be measured | Leverage and liquidity views | High | Obtain the credit agreements and compliance certificates |

| No indenture, credit agreement or Copper World joint venture contract | Legal capacity for distributions, asset transfers and project guarantees cannot be tested; behaviour rests on actions only | Structure, project funding | High | Obtain the executed documents |

| Facility-level availability of the USD 450.0 million revolver and revolver pricing are not printed | The usable amount of the USD 153.7 million and the interest cost of the USD 272.0 million draw are unknown | Liquidity, coverage | High | Obtain the credit agreements |

| Full-year or trailing cash interest is not printed; half-year ratios are timing-distorted | Interest cover over twelve months is Not calculable | Coverage | High | Obtain the FY2025 cash flow statement and coupon dates |
| Nothing dated after 2026-07-29 is supplied | The sanction decision, Q3 2026 results, financing and the Wheaton agreement are Not supplied | All dimensions | High | Supply later filings |

| Audited FY2025 statements and annual information form are not supplied; FY2025 rests on a management release; share count conflicts | The prior-period base and ownership data are second-hand | Leverage trend, ownership | Medium | Obtain the annual exhibits |

| Free cash flow history differs between releases and one trailing cell is misprinted | Cash generation series must name the version | Cash flow quality | Medium | Use the later consistent version and say so |
| Gold share of revenue: management 38% against the filed note at 39.9% of contract revenue | The sensitivity of revenue to gold is uncertain | Business risk | Medium | Ask for the management basis |

| Readiness judgment of this module in the business register is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, not READY | Confidence is held below High | Whole assessment | Medium | Restated here as an inherited limit; resolved only by the legal documents and later filings |
| Ratings, market data, valuation and peer inputs are blank in the context | No market-based view is possible and none is given | Whole assessment | Low | None for this pack |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-5 (evidence trace validation). CP-5 should trace each figure above to the financial base, treat management mine lives, guidance and the stated net debt ceiling as management language, keep the five named conflicts and the gold share conflict open, and not read the ring-fenced ratios as company or covenant measures.

This is the evidence trace and research-integrity review for Hudbay Minerals Inc., as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway, with an evidence cutoff of 2026-11-05. It tests whether the source readiness, financial base, business and transaction register and credit synthesis handoffs rest on the filings they cite, recompute correctly and agree with each other. It changes no credit conclusion and repairs no lineage.
## Sources

Each issuer source is a JSONL text extraction of an SEC filing. The locator `page:N` is the extraction chunk, not the printed page. All seven sources were searched in full for quotes and figures. The sha256 values are the pinned file hashes.
### Issuer sources relied on

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The figures and quotes in the handoffs trace to the filings and recompute correctly, and the modules agree. Committee use is restricted because covenants, debt documents and audited annual statements are missing, not because tracing failed. | Medium | This review was done in the same session as the analysis, so it is not an independent second reviewer. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Every quoted span in the business register was found on the page cited, and all checked ties and ratios recomputed to the printed or stated value. | The numbers a committee would quote can be relied on as labelled. | High |

| Six source conflicts remain unresolved and are carried by name, including a share count difference of 1,312,328 shares and a free cash flow history that changed between releases. | Per-share and cash flow series must name the source version, and no figure may splice versions. | High |

| Two statements are only partly supported: the explanation that half-year interest cover is timing-distorted, and cash of 556.4 described as available to the rest of the group. | These are wording limits; the figures are right, but the interpretations go slightly beyond what the filings state. | Medium |

| Several derived figures in the financial base are stated in text without a line in its calculations table, and one share issue value cites the wrong page. | The derivations are simple and reproduce, so this is a presentation defect, not a reliability defect. | High |

| The latest source is dated 2026-07-29, which is 99 days before the as-of date, and no covenant level or debt document is supplied. | Events and terms that decide the credit view are outside the evidence. | High |
### Evidence trace view

The evidence trace holds. Each material claim in the financial base, the business and transaction register and the credit synthesis was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and the three analytical handoffs agree on every shared figure, period and perimeter label. The synthesis view, a sound profile with Medium confidence and thin committed liquidity as the weak point, follows from the cited basis and is not overstated. Two claims are only partly supported, both as wording rather than figures: that half-year interest cover is distorted by coupon timing, which the filings do not state because coupon dates are not printed, and that cash outside Copper World is available to the rest of the group, which the filings do not say. No claim was found unsupported and no contradiction between modules was found. The integrity verdict for the evaluated set is Restricted, not Committee Ready, because the conclusions that matter most to a creditor rest on documents that are not in the sources: covenant levels and headroom, the indenture and credit agreements, the Copper World contract and plans, the audited FY2025 statements and anything dated after 2026-07-29. Six source conflicts remain open and are named below. The review itself is limited: it was done in the same session as the analysis, from the same extraction text, and page locators are extraction chunks rather than printed pages.
### Evaluated set (inputs and status)
| Input | Status | Evaluated | Notes |
| CP-0 source readiness | Accepted; gate | Quotes and figures rechecked only | Source classes, perimeter and conflicts carried by the other modules |

| CP-1A business and transaction register | Accepted | Yes | Readiness judgment for the synthesis: ready with limitations |
| CP-2 credit synthesis | Accepted on the second attempt | Yes | Confidence Medium, inside the cap set by the upstream limits |
All four are current for the as-of date 2026-11-05 and use USD. The latest source is the Q2 2026 release dated 2026-07-29, 99 days before the as-of date. No input is stale against its own period.
### Material claim register and support review

| Capital commitments 202.6, of which 18.7 not terminable | CP-1 | Q2FS page:29; sums recomputed | Supported | |

| Claims outside debt: leases 53.0, equipment financing 131.3, deferred land payments 102.8, streams, provisions, letters of credit | CP-1 | Q2FS page:15-21 | Supported | Search for factoring, supply chain finance, take-or-pay and retiree medical found none, which I repeated |
| Note guarantees and revolver security exclude Copper World, Mason and Cactus | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 | Q2FS page:18-19 quoted | Supported | |
| Municipal bonds are Copper World LLC obligations guaranteed by the parent | CP-1A, CP-2 | Q2FS page:20 quoted | Supported | |
| Mitsubishi holds 30% of Copper World and owes 180.0 within 18 months | CP-1A | Q2FS page:5, page:9; PR-Q2 page:18 | Supported | |

| Arizona Sonoran acquired for 46,794,082 shares, net identifiable assets 1,267.0, land payments 102.8 | CP-1A | Q2FS page:8, page:16; tie recomputed | Supported | The 1,135.6 value cites page 8 in CP-1; it is printed on pages 4 and 23 |

| Mine lives, production outlook, guidance and the stated net debt ceiling | CP-1A, CP-2 | PR-Q1 page:17-18; PR-Q2 page:2; PR-FY25 page:27 | Supported | Tagged Management Language; not adopted as fact |

| Behaviour read Supportive to Neutral or Mixed; legal capacity not assessed | CP-1A, CP-2 | Rows on debt repurchases, dividend, acquisition funding and guarantee perimeter | Supported | Analyst Interpretation; absence of creditor-adverse actions is an absence statement |

### Citation trace

### Input currency and scale

All inputs are USD. The statements and releases are stated in millions of US dollars; Canadian-dollar items (the C$130.0 million letter of credit facility and the dividend of C$0.01 per share) are labelled. No scale mismatch was found, for example no millions value written for a thousands source.
### Gap propagation
| Upstream limitation | Carried by CP-1 | Carried by CP-1A | Carried by CP-2 |
| Covenant levels not supplied | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Debt documents and guarantor identity missing | Yes | Yes | Yes |

### Findings register
| Finding | Type | Severity | Modules | Effect |

| The explanation that half-year interest cover is timing-distorted is an inference because coupon dates are not printed | Partly supported claim | Minor | CP-1, CP-2 | Wording; the ratios recompute and the caveat is cautious |

| Free cash flow history differs between the February and later releases; the July release misprints one trailing cell; share count differs between the cover and the interim note; municipal bond maturity wording differs; Wheaton stream status unconfirmed; gold share differs from the filed note | Source conflicts, unresolved | Medium | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 | Series and per-share inputs must name the version; none is reconciled |

### Cross-module contradictions

None found. Pairs examined and found consistent: low leverage in CP-1 against thin committed liquidity in CP-2 (both rest on the same 860.2, 1,271.6, 153.7 and 1,044.6); no funded maturity before 2028 in CP-2 against the 272.0 revolver draw at the November 2028 facility maturity in CP-1; the ring-fence described in CP-1A against the ring-fenced ratios in CP-1 and CP-2; the supportive behaviour read in CP-1A against the municipal bond parent guarantee it also records; and the cautious Medium confidence in CP-2 against management's reaffirmed guidance, which CP-1A tags as Management Language and does not adopt.
### Verdict and committee use

Committee status: Restricted. The set may be used by a committee as a source-traced starting view with its stated limits, but not as a basis for conclusions on covenant headroom, legal capacity, project funding or events after 2026-07-29. Nothing was found that blocks use: no unsupported claim, no unresolved cross-module contradiction and no figure that fails to recompute. No numeric confidence score is stated here; the review judges lineage as Directly Sourced for statement and release figures, Calculated for derived figures with inputs shown, and Analyst Inference for the ring-fenced view, the interest timing explanation and the behaviour read. The strongest contrary evidence to the Restricted verdict is that every checkable item passed; what would make it win is receipt of the credit agreements, indenture and Copper World contract, which would convert the open legal and covenant items into checked ones.
## Calculations
